newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended very slightly weaker amid large volumes boosted by bookover deals, dealers said.
The market was weighed in late trade a softer start on Wall Street, they said.
"It has been quite active. We have seen reasonably large trades, a large portion made up by bookover deals," James Scott, equity marketing manager and Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
April's trade figrue was seen as largely positive but had little effect on the equity market. Scott said the main indicators would be credit extension and money supply figures due on Wednesday.
Golds ended flat despite a slightly better bullion price. They initially warmed to the healthier metal around noon but soon retreated.
Nevertheless, dealers said bullion was starting to seem a little more positive which was good enws for stocks.
"The gold price looks like it will go better on palladium prices," said Dominic Rey, Investec Securities international dealer.
The market was seen sideways on Wednesday ahead of the key economic indicators.
The all-share index was down 2.2 points to 7,056.3 points, the industrial index was down 0.3 points to 8,319.3 points and the gold index shed 2.3 points to 1,186.5 points.

Shares in Coca-Cola's South African bottlers Amalgamated Beverage Industries (ABI) and Suncrush rose on Tuesday as investors toasted the demise of Pepsi bottler New Age Beverages which filed for liquidation last Friday.
Suncrush shares ended up 20 cents to 920 cents while ABI climbed 110 cents to 27.70 rand.
SouthWits jumped to a new two year high of 28 cents but settled three cents higher at 25 cents in robust trade. Dealers said the share was enjoying speculation about a possible management change.
Gencor added 55 cents to 19.90 rand with investors believing it stood to gain from current interest in mining stocks after recent mergers and acquisitions in the sector.
Absa shares lost 100 cents to 27.75 rand, continuing to fall after disappointing results announced on Monday.
Near-term equity futures also ended softer after attempting to rise in early trade. They too were weighed by a softer Wall Street open, dealers said.
Gold contracts ended flat but dealers said they were more well-supported than gold shares.
Dealers said players were probably anticipating a run in the gold price.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,405/10 from 6,450, the industrial contract at 8,058/65 from 8,084 and the gold contract at 833/38 from 836.
